h: Bess, Her Hall and the Mill Down the Lane
p: Bess of Hardwick's life reads like a drama series. Born into a modest Derbyshire family, she married four times, climbing higher with each husband until she became Countess of Shrewsbury and one of the richest women in the land. For a while her husband was even jailer to Mary, Queen of Scots. Hardwick was the house she built to show the world exactly how far she'd come, and every window and initial says so.

Once inside, make for the top floor. The High Great Chamber, with its painted plaster frieze of hunting scenes and woodland, is one of the most memorable rooms in the house, and the Long Gallery stretches on and on, hung with tapestries and portraits. Take a moment to look out of those famous windows, too; the views across Derbyshire are part of the show.

Right next door, the ruins of Hardwick Old Hall are looked after by English Heritage, so check what's open on the day. Down on the estate, Stainsby Mill is a working watermill where you can see how flour was ground, a great add-on for kids who like to see how things work.

Allow at least half a day, a full one with a long walk. The hall sits just off junction 29 of the M1, so it's an easy trip from Chesterfield, Mansfield or further afield. If you've still got energy, Bolsover Castle, another dramatic hilltop house, is only a few miles away, and Chesterfield's crooked spire and big outdoor market are perfect for finishing the day.
